source.title: Effects of Non-Uniform Sparsity on Superposition in Toy Models

record.file_problem: The full post and comments are present. The post links to an external Google document and figures whose detailed contents are not included; the text reports some findings from them.
record.tranche_reason: Extends toy-model superposition experiments to non-uniform feature sparsity and reports how feature representation and superposition vary across scenarios.
record.gate_note: The post reports results from its own toy-model experiments. Descriptions of cited figures are included when the text states the finding; no values were inferred from figures. The linked Google document is not part of the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post studies feature superposition in the hidden layer of the Toy Models ReLU output model (h=Wx, 5→2 and 80→20). That hidden layer is linear and has no privileged basis, so 'dedicated dimension vs superposition' is not a measure of individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs. No neuron-level polysemanticity rate or share is reported in any model. The study also never compares against a no-capacity-pressure control, so it cannot test V3's causal claim that polysemantic neurons arise from superposition. It is related mechanism work on superposition under non-uniform sparsity, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author finds that non-uniform sparsity never represents all 5 features and lowers a Frobenius-norm representation proxy relative to uniform sparsity. The split between dedicated and superposed features varies with how sparsity pairs with importance. From Case 4 the author infers that importance matters more than sparsity for dedicated dimensions. They admit they could not determine the governing combination and lack intuition for Case 4.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a ReLU output toy model similar to the referenced toy-model setup, but investigates non-uniform rather than uniform feature sparsity and varies feature-importance patterns.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary across four feature-sparsity and feature-importance patterns. The author also ran eight random-seed instances per scenario.

fits_no_version.finding: In the 5→2 ReLU output toy model, non-uniform feature sparsity never yields all 5 features represented, unlike uniform sparsity. Whether represented features get dedicated directions or are superposed depends on how sparsity is paired with importance: Case 1 has most dedicated directions, Case 2 has all superposed, Case 3 is mixed. With equal importance (Case 4), the densest features go unrepresented.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy superposition models, the pattern of superposition depends on the joint distribution of feature sparsity and importance, not on sparsity level alone.

fits_no_version.finding: A Frobenius-norm proxy for total representation is lower under every non-uniform sparsity case (4.98–6.6) than under uniform sparsity (7.55) in the 80→20 model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-uniform sparsity reduces the number of features a toy bottleneck model represents.

record.problems: The study uses toy models rather than trained image or language models. The post reports eight instances per scenario but gives no uncertainty estimates. The Frobenius norm is only a proxy for feature representation, not a direct measure of superposition. Some detailed figures are available only through external links not included in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No textual results bearing on V3 were intentionally left out. Detailed figure contents and the linked Google document could not be extracted from the supplied text.

untested.parts: No neuron-level polysemanticity is measured (the hidden layer has no privileged basis), and there is no control without capacity pressure to establish causation.
No setting with enough neurons for every feature; seed effects are noted only anecdotally.
No activation, architecture or regularization comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with V3 supports and limits_scope labels is overturned. Superposition in the ReLU output model's linear hidden layer is not neuron polysemanticity, and no capacity-pressure contrast is made. The post is an unreviewed LessWrong post with no uncertainty estimates. Figures and the linked Google document are not available.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and mixed visual inputs.
Transformer language-model MLP neurons and tokens or contexts.

The experiments examine superposition in toy ReLU models with more input features than hidden dimensions, but do not isolate whether this capacity difference causes superposition compared with a model without capacity pressure.
Initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
Activation-function or architecture comparisons, regularization changes, and performance costs.
Whether mixed features share a coherent underlying job.
How the measured activation range or explanation-scoring method affects whether a neuron is classified as polysemantic.

rows.value: Maximum of 4; the count hovers around 3 in many scenarios. All 5 features were never represented in the non-uniform-sparsity scenarios.
rows.note: The count is summarized across scenarios rather than reported separately for each one.
rows.check: This counts features represented in a non-privileged linear hidden space. It is not a neuron polysemanticity measure, and no V3 causal contrast is made.
